title: Claude Managed Agents Q&A: Evals, CI/CD and Multi-Tenancy (Part 4 of 4) — Anthropic
talk_summary: This is a Q&A session covering CI/CD for agent definitions via YAML+CLI, eval harness practices, multi-tenant workspace isolation, sandbox resource customization, and long-running session patterns. Most content is Claude-platform-specific, but a few mechanisms (YAML-defined agent configs synced via CI, PR-triggered multi-agent review, sandbox self-validation, exit-criteria loops) are directly copyable.

takeaways.technique: YAML-defined agent resources synced via CI
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent definitions (system prompt, model, tools) live as YAML in the repo; a CLI applies them to the platform, so CI updates all agent definitions on change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can put your uh long-term uh resources in YAML in your code base and then build um CICD to basically update the Ancho with Ancho CLI using those YAMLs

takeaways.what_they_do: On each PR, kick off multiple review sessions with sub-agents to evaluate the diff and find bugs, reducing per-PR human time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: on PR, it kicks off one, two, three, many sessions with many sub-agents to evaluate what has changed and find bugs

takeaways.technique: Agent self-validation in sandbox as QA
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the app inside the sandbox and have the agent exercise it (browser) to validate its own change before handing off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You you can run your application in the sandbox as well and have Claude self-validate the changes that it made

takeaways.what_they_do: Define an explicit exit criteria/rubric and let the agent iterate until it matches, rather than a fixed step budget.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you define an exit criteria and Claude will just keep going until it meets that criteria

takeaways.what_they_do: Build eval datasets from past real sessions, score them, and iterate on data quality because ill-defined evals give meaningless 100%.
takeaways.evidence_quote: look at like your historical sessions and like what results you got and then sort of try to score it

takeaways.technique: Pluggable sandbox providers for resource needs
takeaways.what_they_do: Default sandboxes are uniform; for GPU/memory needs they swap in self-hosted providers (Modal, Daytona, E2B) via cookbooks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you want to do custom resource allocations for your sandbox, you would use self-hosted sandboxes
